Definition
In this lesson you should examine the concept of frequency modulation and frequency modulated signals. _
INTRODUCTIONM
Frequency modulation, FM, is another method of signal processing and was developed around 1936.
Today, most all home radios have the capability to receive both AM and FM signals.
FM communication systems have several advantages over AM systems. For example, FM is less noisy, as you probably already know.
Also, FM signals are sent in stereo, or two signals, one for each side, left and right. AM is not normally transmitted in stereo.
Let's begin the lesson on FREQUENCY MODULATION............................
LESSON MENU
FREQUENCY MODULATION
Frequency Modulation, FM, is used to convey information from a source to a destination through a transmission medium, just like AM.
DISCUSSION
Frequency Modulation is a signal processing technique that modifies a carrier signal by the information signal, just like AM.
Without this modification the information signal could not be sent, just like AM.
The name frequency modulation is derived from how the carrier signal is modified; by frequency. The amplitude of the carrier signal remains constant, unlike AM.
In transmitter signal processing, a constant amplitude carrier signal is developed by an oscillator.
The carrier signal is then fed to an FM modulator circuit.m
The second input to the modulator circuit is the information signal.
The modulator circuit causes the frequency of the carrier signal to change according to the amplitude of the information signal.
As the information signal's amplitude increases, the carrier frequency is increased.
As the information signal's amplitude decreases, the carrier frequency is decreased.
Note that the carrier signal and frequency of the information signal have the same rate of change.
The resultant FM signal is then transmitted through the transmission medium, normally air, but could be through wire or fiber optic cables.
In receiver signal processing, the transmitted FM signal is picked up through a tuning process and the information signal recovered.
The tuning circuits allow you to choose which one of the many FM signals to process.
The detector circuits separate the carrier signal from the information signal.
The information signal is then sent to amplifiers for further processing.

CARRIER FREQUENCY
As in AM systems, the carrier frequency in FM systems must be higher than the information frequency.
Unlike AM systems, there is no rule of thumb to follow.
The carrier frequency must be high enough to allow the full extent of frequency changes caused by the changes in amplitude of the information signal.
This includes the sideband frequencies. You will see in FM the number of sidebands can theoretically be infinite. Remember in AM there are only two, upper and lower.
However, the carrier frequency for FM should be 5 MHz or higher. This is not a problem since the lower carrier frequencies are used in AM systems.
FM radio uses carrier frequencies between 88 and 108 MHz. TV uses frequencies of 54 to 88 MHz, 174 to 216 MHz and 470 to
MODULATION INDEX AND DEVIATION RATIO
The modulation index and deviation ratio of a FM signal determines the extent and the rate of modulation. It is similar to the percent modulation in AM systems.
The difference between AM and FM is that the AM percent modulation ranges from 0% to 100%. The FM modulation index and ratio has much higher values.
The formula for modulation index is the frequency deviation (fd) divided by the modulating frequency (fm).
For example, FM broadcast stations are allowed a frequency deviation of 75 kHz, if a 4 kHz audio signal causes full deviation, then the modulation index is 18.75.
Notice that the modulation index is changed when the information signal frequency changes.
Also, notice that changes in the frequency deviation also change the modulation index.
In other words, the frequency of the modulation signal and the amount of frequency deviation will change the modulation index.

For example, if the information signal is voice, 40 Hz to 4 kHz, and using the 75 kHz limit for deviation, the deviation ratio equals 18.75.
If the information signal increases slightly by 2 kHz, the deviation ratio is the same because the signal could rise to 4 kHz.

SIDEBANDS
The major difference is that FM can have many sideband frequencies and AM only has two.
Remember, like AM waveforms, FM waveforms are not made of the carrier frequency and the modulating frequency.
AM and FM waveforms are complex waveforms that are a combination of the carrier frequency and sideband frequencies.
The many sidebands in FM waveforms are due to the numerous frequency shifts produced by the modulating signal.
Consequently, in theory, FM waveforms can have an infinite number of sidebands.
But, many of the higher order sidebands contain a very small amount of power and therefore can be ignored.
The graph below illustrates that as the modulation index increases, the number of significant sidebands increase, and the amplitude of the carrier and sidebands change.
The graph is called the Bessel Function, named after the person who developed it.
At a modulation index of 0, no modulation, the carrier signal has an amplitude of 100% and there are no sideband frequencies.

BANDWIDTH
The bandwidth of a communication system is the highest frequency used in the system. Just as with AM, FM has a bandwidth also.
In the AM system, the bandwidth of the AM waveform is twice the modulating frequency, or the range of frequencies between the lower and upper sidebands.
FM is a little more complex since there are normally more than two sidebands.
The bandwidth of an FM waveform is the modulating frequency times 2 times the number of sidebands.

As in AM systems, noise in FM systems are variations in amplitude caused by; transmission medium, outside interference or thermal noise.
However, unlike AM systems, the FM signal can be limited to reduce all amplitude variations.
Remember, the information of an FM signal is determined by frequency variations. Amplitude variations are used in AM systems.
This is the big advantage of FM systems over AM systems, noise can be eliminated.
